newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end a shade higher, await elections.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end a shade higher, await elections.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended a shade higher in Thursday's session after wandering narrowly in both negative and positive territory throughout the day. Brokers said investors were waiting for the Lower House of parliament elections which will be held on Sunday.
The 225-issue Nikkei average inched up 26.55 points or 0.12 percent to 21,423.74. Its December futures were up 70 points at 21,500.
"The market jumped on election speculation earlier in the week, but the election is only days away now and it is stunting activity," said Kenzo Doi, strategist at Kokusai Securities.

Haseko Corp closed 15 yen higher at 405. Brokers said media reports that the company is forecast to post a parent current profit of 1.8 billion yen in the six months to September 30, after suffering a loss in the same period a year ago, gave investors confidence to buy.
Keisei Electric Railway chugged higher on speculation that the listing of Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land may be drawing near, brokers said.
The shares, the most heavily traded issue, ended 40 yen higher at 1,170, with a volume of 7.839 million shares.

Mitsubishi Motors gained seven yen to 958 yen, supported by the yen's weakness against the dollar and a newly developed engine, traders said. The eighth most heavily traded issue had a volume of 2.414 million.

Roland Corp surged 400 yen to 2,400 yen on the Osaka Securities Exchange, propelled by news that the electronic keyboard instrument maker would provide Microsoft Corp with digital data for musical sounds in personal computer software, traders said.
The over-the-counter index shed 0.10 point or 0.01 percent, reaching 1,531.69 by 0707 GMT.--M.Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk
